questions.question: A1 alone can do a work in 12 days and A2 alone can do the same work in 15 days. With help of A3, they finish the same work in 5 days. In how many days A3 alone can do the same work ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A1 does the work in 12 days.

A2 does the same work in 15 days.

A1, A2, and A3 together do the work in 5 days.

**Formula:**

Work = Time × Efficiency

**Calculation:**

Total work = LCM(12, 15, 5) = 60 units

Efficiency of A1 = 60/12 = 5

Efficiency of A2 = 60/15 = 4

Efficiency of A1 + A2 + A3 = 60/5 = 12

Efficiency of A3 = (Efficiency of A1 + A2 + A3) - (Efficiency of A1 + A2)

⇒ Efficiency of A3 = 12 - 9 = 3

Time taken by A3 to complete the work = 60/3 = 20 days

**Therefore, A3 alone can do the work in 20 days.**

questions.question: Mahesh. Suresh and Raju together can complete a work in 18 days. Mahesh and Suresh together can complete the same work in 72 days. Raju alone can finish the same work in how many days?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Mahesh, Suresh, and Raju together do the work in 18 days.

Mahesh and Suresh together do the same work in 72 days.

Formula:

Work = Time × Efficiency

Calculation:

Total work = LCM(18, 72) = 72 units

Efficiency of Mahesh, Suresh, and Raju = 72/18 = 4

Efficiency of Mahesh and Suresh = 72/72 = 1

Efficiency of Raju = (Efficiency of Mahesh, Suresh, and Raju) - (Efficiency of Mahesh and Suresh)

⇒ Efficiency of A3 = 4 - 1 = 3

Time taken by Raju to complete the work = 72/3 = 24 days

Therefore, Raju alone can do the work in 24 days.

questions.question: What will be the length of longest diagonal of the cuboid having length 13 cm width 11 cm and height 20 cm?
questions.solution:

Length of cuboid = 13 cm

Width of cuboid = 11 cm

Height of cuboid = 20 cm

**Formula: **

The longest diagonal of a cuboid = √(length² + width² + height²)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Diagonal = √(13² + 11² + 20²)

⇒ Diagonal = √(169 + 121 + 400)

Diagonal = √(690) = 26.2 cm

**Therefore, the length of the longest diagonal of the cuboid is approximately 26.27 cm.**

questions.solution:

The set of numbers is 30, 45, 150.

**Formula:**

Highest Common Factor (HCF) is the largest number that divides each of the given numbers.

**Calculation:**

The factors of 30 are 1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 15, 30.

The factors of 45 are 1, 3, 5, 9, 15, 45.

The factors of 150 are 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 25, 30, 50, 75, 150.

The common factors of 30, 45, and 150 are 1, 3, 5, 15.

HCF = 15

**Therefore, the HCF of the numbers 30, 45, and 150 is 15.**

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 2000 will become Rs. 2400 in 12 months at some rate of simple interest. Find the rate of interest per annum.

questions.question: A shopkeeper earns 20% profit on his goods. He lost 20% of his goods during a theft. What is his profit or loss percent?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Profit percentage = 20%
Percentage of goods lost = 20%

**Formula:**

The formula for calculating loss percentage is (Loss / Cost Price) × 100.

**Calculation:**

Initial Cost Price (CP) = 1 unit (for simplicity)

Initial Selling Price (SP) = CP + (Profit % of CP) ⇒ 1 + 0.2 × 1 = 1.2 units

Percentage of goods remaining = 100% - 20% = 80%

CP of remaining goods = 0.8 × 1 = 0.8 units

SP of remaining goods = 0.8 × 1.2 = 0.96 units

Loss = CP - SP ⇒ 1 - 0.96 = 0.04 units

Loss percentage = (Loss / CP) × 100 ⇒ (0.04 / 1) × 100 = 4%

**Therefore, the shopkeeper has a loss of 4%.**

questions.question: The ratio of the outer and the inner circumference of a circular path is 17 ∶ 15. If path is 40 metres wide, then what is the radius of the inner circle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The ratio of circumferences of two circles is identical to the ratio of their radii.

Ratio of outer radius (R) to inner radius (r) = 17 ∶ 15

Width of the path in ratio units = 17 − 15 = 2 units.

Given width = 40 metres, so 2 units = 40 metres ⇒ 1 unit = 20 metres.

Inner radius = 15 units = 15 × 20 = 300 metres.

**∴ The correct answer is 300 metres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of outer and inner circumference = 17 ∶ 15

Width of the path = 40 metres

**Formula Used:**

Circumference of a circle = 2×π×r

Width of circular path = R − r

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/901a6739e9dc59f8882b395fec41f837af89839e1d5def8de74be8db74beb14f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the outer radius be R and the inner radius be r.

⇒ Ratio of circumferences = (2×π×R) ÷ (2×π×r)

⇒ R / r = 17 / 15

⇒ Let R = 17x and r = 15x

⇒ Width of the circular path = Outer Radius − Inner Radius

⇒ 17x − 15x = 40

⇒ 2x = 40

⇒ x = 20

⇒ Inner radius (r) = 15x = 15 × 20 = 300 metres

**∴ The correct answer is 300 metres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Circular Path

The total area located strictly between two concentric circles is given by Area = π×(R² − r²), where R and r are the respective outer and inner radii.

Length of an Arc

An arc is a fraction of the full circumference. The length is determined by the central angle θ: (θ ÷ 360) × 2πr.

Area of a Sector

The region bounded by two radii and an adjoining arc is called a sector. Its area is: (θ ÷ 360) × πr².

questions.question: Find compound interest on Rs. 8000 at 15% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = Rs. 8000

Rate of interest (R) = 15% per annum

Time (T) = 2 years

**Formula:**

Compound Interest = P(1 + R/100)² - P

**Calculation:**

⇒ Compound Interest = 8000(1 + 15/100)² - 8000

⇒ Compound Interest = 8000(1.15)² - 8000

Compound Interest = Rs. 2580

**Therefore, the compound interest on Rs. 8000 at 15% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually, is Rs. 2580.**

questions.question: A car has to cover a distance of 288 km in 20 hours. If it covers half of the journey in 1/5th of the time, find the speed to cover the remaining distance in the time left.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Remaining Distance** = 288 ÷ 2 = 144 km.

**Remaining Time** = 20 × (1 − 1/5) = 20 × 4/5 = 16 hours.

**Required Speed** = 144 ÷ 16 = 9 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 km/hr.**

**Formula Used:** Speed = Distance ÷ Time

⇒ **First half distance** = 288 ÷ 2 = 144 km.

⇒ **Remaining distance** = 288 − 144 = 144 km.

⇒ **Time taken for first half** = 1/5 × 20 = 4 hours.

⇒ **Remaining time** = 20 − 4 = 16 hours.

⇒ **Speed for remaining journey** = 144 ÷ 16 = 9 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 km/hr.**

questions.question: An image which can be obtained on a screen is called a ____________.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In optics, a **real image** is an image that is formed when rays converge at a specific point.
 
• They can be projected onto a screen or a photographic film.
 
• Real images can be produced by concave mirrors and converging** lenses, assuming the object is placed further from the mirror or lens than the focal point, and this image is inverted.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vector Image:**

 
 
• This refers to a type of digital graphic that uses mathematical formulas to render its design, instead of using pixel data like raster images.
 
• Because of this, vector images can be scaled to any size without loss of resolution. 
 
 
 
• **Virtual Image:**
 
 
• In the field of optics, a virtual image is an image formed when the outgoing rays from a point on the object always diverge.
 
• The image appears to be located at the point of apparent divergence.
 
• Because the rays never really converge, a virtual image cannot be projected onto a screen.
 
• Examples of virtual images include the image seen in a single plane mirror, the image seen through a magnifying glass, or the image seen in a camera viewfinder.
 
 
 
• **Spectral Image: **
 
 
• A spectral image is an image whose pixels contain information from across the electromagnetic spectrum.
 
• These images are captured by spectral imaging techniques which capture the entire spectrum in each pixel.
 
• These images are used for various purposes like remote sensing, astrophysics, etc.

questions.question: In biology, the term "IVF" stands for __________.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In Vitro Fertilization (IVF)** is a type of assisted reproductive technology (ART) used to help individuals or couples conceive a child.
 
• The term** "in vitro"** is a Latin term meaning** "in glass,"** referring to the test tubes used in laboratories, although the actual process now uses more advanced technology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here is a basic outline of the IVF process:
 
• **Ovarian stimulation and monitoring: **
 
 
• The woman is given hormonal medications to stimulate the ovaries to produce multiple eggs instead of the single egg typically released during a menstrual cycle.
 
• Regular ultrasound and blood tests are performed to monitor the development of the follicles (fluid-filled ovarian sacs that contain the eggs).
 
 
 
• **Egg retrieval: **
 
 
• Once the eggs mature, a medical procedure known as follicular aspiration is performed to retrieve them.
 
• A thin needle is inserted through the vagina and into the ovary under ultrasound guidance, and the fluid in the follicles is aspirated.
 
 
 
• **Insemination and Fertilization: **
 
 
• The eggs are combined with sperm in a petri dish and incubated overnight. If traditional IVF doesn't seem promising, a single sperm may be injected directly into an egg, a process known as intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI).
 
 
 
• **Embryo culture: **
 
 
• The fertilized eggs (now embryos) are monitored for growth.
 
• The goal is to grow these embryos for about five days until they reach a stage called the blastocyst stage.
 
 
 
• **Embryo transfer: **
 
 
• Once the embryos are ready, one or more are transferred into the woman's uterus through the cervix using a thin catheter.
 
• If an embryo implants in the lining of the uterus and grows, a pregnancy results.

• **Xanthophyll:**

• It absorbs **light** in a** wavelength range** that **chlorophyll **cannot, and helps protect the plant from the harmful effects of excessive light energy.

questions.question: For a bank, the main liability is the __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**deposits**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The key business of the banks is to accept different types of deposits from the public and then lend these funds to the borrowers.
 
 
• This is called Financial intermediation.
 
 
 
• In terms of the banks, the deposits represent the “liabilities” of the banks while loans advanced and investments made by banks represent their “assets”.
 
• The deposit itself is a liability owed by the bank to the depositor.
 
• Bank deposits refer to this liability rather than to the actual funds that have been deposited.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• High Powered Money:

 
 
• The total liability of the monetary authority of the country, RBI, is called the monetary base or high-powered money.
 
• It consists of currency (notes and coins in circulation with the public and vault cash of commercial banks) and deposits held by the Government of India and commercial banks with RBI.
 
 
 
• If a member of the public produces a currency note to RBI the latter must pay her value equal to the figure printed on the note. Similarly, the deposits are also refundable by RBI on-demand from deposit-holders.
 
• These items are claims which the general public, government, or banks have on RBI and hence are considered to be the liability of RBI. RBI acquires assets against these liabilities.
 
• This can be understood by an example. Suppose RBI purchases gold or dollars worth Rs 5. It pays for the gold or foreign exchange by issuing currency to the seller. The currency in circulation in the economy thus goes up by Rs 5, an item that shows up on the liability side of the balance sheet. The value of the acquired assets, also equal to Rs 5, is entered under the appropriate head on the Assets side.
 
• Similarly, RBI acquires debt bonds or securities issued by the government and pays the government by issuing currency in return. It issues loans to commercial banks in a similar fashion.
 
• However, the most important role of RBI is as the controller of money supply and credit creation in the economy.
 
• RBI is the independent authority for conducting monetary policy in the best interests of the economy – it increases or decreases the supply of high-powered money in the economy and creates incentives or disincentives for the commercial banks to give loans or credits to investors.
